NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular business
  hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a recording is
  available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and
  Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received
  before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 9, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR HUFF at 7:08 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Scouts from Troop 783: Tyler Coleman, Blake Holdsworth, Liam Kilcullen, Jack
Konner, Luke Stenberg, Ryan Stenberg, Assistant Scout Master Robert Kilcullen and
Committee Chair Stacey Nozaki.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Stegura

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF OUTGOING PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSIONER KIRK
  RETZ

MAYOR HUFF presented Kirk Retz with a Certificate of Recognition for seven years of service
on the Park and Activities Commission.

**COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN joined the meeting at 7:18 p.m.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2023 "MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR HUFF declared May 2023 as Mental Health Awareness Month.

C.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2023 "MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH
  AWARENESS MONTH"

MAYOR HUFF presented the Proclamation to Dr. Ellie Berkowitz-Handler and Ashley
McCarthy from Governing Council of Maternal Mental Health NOW, declaring May 2023 as
Maternal Mental Health Awareness Month.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ spoke personally about the importance of Maternal Mental
Health and resources available.

D.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 20, 2023 "NATIONAL KIDS TO PARKS DAY"

MAYOR HUFF declared May 20, 2023 as National Kids to Parks Day.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 9, 2023
 E.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2023 “WILDFIRE PREPAREDNESS MONTH”

MAYOR HUFF presented the Proclamation to Los Angeles County Fire Department Battalion
Chief Svoboda and members from Fire Station 2, declaring May 2023 as Wildfire
Preparedness Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-I AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF APRIL 2023

  APPROVED WARRANTS 66196 THROUGH 66248 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $619,170.82, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040423 THROUGH
  040523; 65325 VOID; IN THE AMOUNT OF $90,594.75 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $709,765.57 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MINUTES OF APRIL 25, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 25, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MARCH 27, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 17,
  2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION - PAGLIANO PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT BY
  KORMEX CONSTRUCTION INC.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  DESIGNATION OF CITY’S AGENTS BY TITLE AND SIGNATURE AUTHORITY TO
  OBTAIN FEDERAL AND/OR STATE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE THROUGH THE
  CALIFORNIA OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES (CITY RESOLUTION NO.
  2544)

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF APRIL 28, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 9, 2023
 6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AWARD OF A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT FOR THE PETER WEBER
  EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) approve a Public Works Contract, as to
  form by the City Attorney, in the amount of $138,337.80 with CXT Inc. for the
  purchase and installation of a new restroom unit at the PWEC; 2) authorize the
  allocation of Park and Facilities Fees in the amount of $143,587.80 for Fiscal Year
  2023-2024.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Management Analyst Slawson explained the timeline for the project which is estimated to be
completed by the end of summer, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) APPROVE A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT, AS TO FORM BY THE CITY
  ATTORNEY, IN THE AMOUNT OF $138,337.80 WITH CXT INC. FOR THE
  PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF A NEW RESTROOM UNIT AT THE
  PWEC; AND 2) AUTHORIZE THE ALLOCATION OF PARK AND FACILITIES
  FEES IN THE AMOUNT OF $143,587.80 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

B.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 746 AMENDING AND RESTATING
  CHAPTER 6.04 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO ANIMAL REGULATIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Receive Public Testimony; 2) Discuss
  the proposed changes to Chapter 6.04 of the RHEMC as stated in Ordinance No.
  746; 3) Introduce for First Reading Ordinance No. 746 amending and restating
  Chapter 6.04 of the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code pertaining to animal
  regulations; and 4) Continue Ordinance No. 746 to the next regular City Council
  meeting for Second Reading and Adoption.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. 746 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 6.04 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE PERTAINING TO ANIMAL REGULATIONS; AND CONTINUED
  ORDINANCE NO. 746 TO THE NEXT REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FOR SECOND READING AND ADOPTION.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 9, 2023
   AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 746 by title.

C.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 747 TO ADD CHAPTER 8.42 (SINGLE-USE
  FOODWARE ACCESSORIES) TO TITLE 8 (HEALTH AND SAFETY) OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Receive Public Testimony; 2) Discuss
  the proposed addition of Chapter 8.42 of the RHEMC as stated in Ordinance No. 747;
  3) Introduce Ordinance No. 747 for First Reading; and 4) Continue Ordinance No.
  747 to the next regular City Council meeting for Second Reading and Adoption.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material.)

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ confirmed that restaurant owners can choose to offer single-use
foodware at customers’ requests.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. 747 ADDING
  CHAPTER 8.42 TO TITLE 8 (HEALTH AND SAFETY) OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO SINGLE-USE FOODWARE
  ACCESSORIES; AND CONTINUED ORDINANCE NO. 747 TO THE NEXT
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR SECOND READING AND
  ADOPTION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 747 by title.

D.  LEGISLATIVE UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ confirmed that staff will review all bills before sending any
support or opposition letters on urgent bills not brought to the City Council.

City Manager Grammer clarified that individual Council Members may take personal positions
not on behalf of the City, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 9, 2023
 10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER attended the West Basin Water District’s Water Issues
Forum on May 5.

MAYOR HUFF attended the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) General
Assembly along with COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN last week.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported out regarding the SCAG General Assembly, and
noted he and many other Council Members will be attending the California Contract Cities
Association’s Annual Municipal Seminar May 18 – 21.

MAYOR HUFF participated on the strategic planning Advisory Council for the the Palos Verdes
Land Conservancy last week, and also met with Congressman Ted Lieu along with the Land
Conservancy at the Nature Center to discuss its future plans and development.

MAYOR HUFF was also re-elected to the Board of Directors of California Association of
Councils of Governments (CALCOG).

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ spoke about John Pagliano, the resident and longtime Park and
Activities Commissioner the Perimeter Pathway Project was named in honor of.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  APPOINTMENT OF PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSIONER

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPOINT ZACHARY HOLDSWORTH TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

MAYOR HUFF reminded the public about the upcoming Mayor’s Breakfast Ride on
Saturday, May 13 at 8:00 a.m.

At 8:11 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to Tuesday, May 23, 2023,
at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 9, 2023
